unrecognized_device.title: Unrecognized device
unrecognized_device.description:
The device at {host} reports itself as {device}, which is not a UNAS or UNVR model this integration knows. Installing onto another UniFi console (a UDM, for example) runs the monitoring scripts there and mixes its data with your NAS.

If you are sure this is your NAS, pick its model to continue.

init.title: UniFi UNAS Options
init.description: How often the UNAS publishes its metrics. Lower values update faster but add load on the UNAS. Applied right away, without a restart.

duplicate_publishers.title: Multiple devices publishing to the same MQTT topic
duplicate_publishers.description:
More than one device is publishing UniFi UNAS data to the same MQTT topic prefix. This usually means the integration's SSH host was reconfigured at some point and the previous device is still running orphaned scripts, which will corrupt sensor values by mixing data from both devices.

Machine IDs seen: {machine_ids}

To identify which device is the orphan, compare the machine IDs above against `/etc/machine-id` on your UNAS. Then SSH into the other device(s) and run:

```
systemctl disable --now unas_monitor fan_control
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/unas_monitor.service /etc/systemd/system/fan_control.service
rm -rf /root/unifi_unas /root/unas_monitor.py /root/fan_control.sh
systemctl daemon-reload
```

This warning will clear automatically once only one device is publishing.

ssh_unavailable.title: UNAS SSH connection unavailable
ssh_unavailable.description:
Home Assistant has been unable to reach your UniFi UNAS at `{host}` over SSH for over 10 minutes. Monitoring continues over MQTT, but the integration cannot check, update or redeploy the scripts on the UNAS, and backup controls are unavailable.

Check that the UNAS is powered on and reachable, and that SSH is enabled. If the UNAS rejects the login instead, Home Assistant asks for the credentials again.

deploy_failed.title: Could not deploy the UNAS scripts
deploy_failed.description:
Home Assistant could not install or update the monitor and fan control scripts on your UniFi UNAS at `{host}`. It keeps retrying in the background, up to once an hour.

Last error: `{error}`

The fan keeps running on whatever controls it now: the previous scripts if they are still installed, otherwise UniFi's own fan control. Press **Reinstall Scripts** on the UNAS device to retry right away. This message clears by itself once a deploy succeeds.

host_key_changed.title: UniFi UNAS SSH host key changed

confirm.title: Re-pin the UniFi UNAS SSH host key
confirm.description: The SSH host key presented by the NAS at {host} no longer matches the pinned key. If you expected this (for example after a firmware reinstall), select **Submit** to trust the new key and re-pin it. If you did not expect it, cancel and investigate before continuing.

stale_topics.title: Leftover MQTT topics from removed UNAS installs

confirm.title: Clear leftover MQTT topics
confirm.description:
Your MQTT broker still keeps {count} retained topics under {roots}. They were left behind by UniFi UNAS installs that have since been removed (versions before 0.10 could leave an `offline` status behind), and nothing is publishing to them.

Select **Submit** to clear them. Skip this if another Home Assistant instance uses this integration with the same broker, since its topics would show up here while its NAS is offline.
